brand.purpose: Product name in the fixed header rail. Appears once.

readout.purpose: The primary instrument value. At most one per panel.

title.purpose: Control labels, tab labels, metric names.

micro.purpose: Uppercase plate text: badges and the provenance table header. Provenance tags sit at 10.5px.

table.purpose: Dense fleet table body, 11px tabular. Fleet table only.

shadows.name: floating-glass
shadows.purpose: HUD panels and popovers suspended over the live 3D render, always paired with a backdrop blur. The honesty popover deepens it to 0.4 alpha.

shadows.name: tone-ring
shadows.purpose: Active state of a tone-carrying card. An inset hairline in the tone colour, never a glow.

shadows.name: selection-ring
shadows.purpose: Selected sensor card (with a Machine Yellow border); the matching in-scene label takes a Machine Yellow outer ring.

shadows.name: label-drop
shadows.purpose: In-scene label pills, so text stays legible against arbitrary geometry. Active labels use 0 4px 14px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4).

shadows.name: status-dot-halo
shadows.purpose: The 9px status dot only, in the tone it reports.

shadows.name: brand-mark
shadows.purpose: The OG mark in the header rail. The only glow that is not a state response.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default transition for background and border-colour on interactive elements.

motion.name: ease-panel
motion.purpose: Drawer collapse and resize. The only timing function named in the system.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All CSS transitions are removed; 3D easing alphas resolve to 1 so scene motion snaps to its target.

breakpoints.name: hud-trim
breakpoints.purpose: Header tagline and the bottom-left HUD stack are removed entirely.

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.purpose: View stacks vertically; the drawer becomes a full-width band capped at 45% of view height; dashboard sheets drop to one column.

breakpoints.name: touch-shell
breakpoints.purpose: Two-row 108px header with a 44px scrolling nav; 44px minimum targets on every control; wheel view scrolls as a column with the dock in flow.

narrative.overview:
Every surface in this product behaves like a measuring instrument, not like an application. A gauge does not decorate its reading; it declares its uncertainty. The oil level arrives wrapped in a confidence band because the reading has one. Every figure carries a provenance tag - VERIFIED, DERIVED, ASSUMPTION - because a number without a source is a liability on equipment a person is accountable for.

Machine yellow on graphite carries that idea physically. The yellow is Komatsu's own paint - komatsuYellow in the 3D palette is the same value as the brand token - so the interface and the machine are literally the same colour. Graphite is the unlit pit the instrument sits in.

Density is deliberate and high. This is read by an engineer comparing a trend against a threshold, so information per square centimetre outranks whitespace. The system refuses the entire vocabulary of reassurance: no progress theatre, no celebratory motion, no soft-card dashboard idiom. The instrument is quiet at rest. Its job is to be believed when it speaks.
keyCharacteristics: Machine yellow as identity, Instrument amber as caution - two near-identical yellows that never trade roles.
Depth by tone in the shell, by hairline border in the data surfaces: two documented materials.
Provenance as a first-class visual component, alongside colour and type size.
Tabular figures everywhere, so nothing jitters while it updates.
Flat at rest. Shadow is a response to state, never decoration.
Status never travels on colour alone: every tone ships with a word, a dot, or a numbered marker beside it.
Numbers are localised: Spanish reads with a decimal comma, English with a point, one formatter for both.

rules.name: The Two-Yellow Rule
rules.body: Machine Yellow is who we are; Instrument Amber is what we warn about. Neither ever takes the other's job. If a state can only be distinguished by swapping which yellow it uses, the state needs a second signal - a label, a ring, or a position.

rules.name: The Machine-Wears-Its-Own-Paint Rule
rules.body: Machine Yellow is simultaneously the brand colour and the machine's paint in the 3D scene, and that overlap is intentional, not a coincidence to be normalised away.

rules.name: The Status Palette Is Closed
rules.body: Signal Green, Motion Blue, Instrument Amber, Caution Orange and Critical Red carry fixed meanings. They are never reassigned for decoration.

rules.name: The Sensor Identity Rule
rules.body: Sensor identity uses neutral Annotation-colored numbered rings (24px beside a sensor card, 18px inside the in-scene label pill), never the closed status palette. Machine Yellow may indicate selection; status colors communicate machine condition only.

rules.name: The Word-Beside-Colour Rule
rules.body: A status tone is never the only carrier of its meaning. The analyzer-outage notice pairs a full red border with a red dot and a role="alert" sentence; the RUL panel pairs its horizon tone with a role="status" text cue; the fleet table writes Alert or Normal and lists the offending channels in words. If a new surface can only be read by its hue, it needs a label.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that changes over time carries tabular-nums, so a figure holds its column while it updates.

rules.name: The Fixed-Pixel Rule
rules.body: The system is absolute pixels - no rem, no html font-size - so a readout occupies the same width at every density.

rules.name: The Locale-Decimal Rule
rules.body: Every displayed figure goes through formatNumber(value, lang, digits): en-US for English, es-CL for Spanish (decimal comma), never grouping separators, and a fixed digit count per quantity so the column width does not move when the language switches. Do not interpolate a raw number into copy.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Shadow appears only as a response to state - focus, active tone, or a panel genuinely floating above a render.

rules.name: The Glass Is Not Frosted, It Is Situated
rules.body: Backdrop blur marks a panel floating over live 3D content. Do not blur a panel sitting on flat graphite; there is nothing behind it to situate.

dos: Do carry the provenance of every figure into the layout - a tag, a badge, a footnote naming the source file and the assumption it rests on.
Do use Machine Yellow for identity and selection, and Instrument Amber for caution, and keep them in their lanes.
Do mark live data and demo data differently, and label which is which, even when the backend is healthy.
Do let density serve the comparison being made. An engineer reading a trend against a threshold wants the pixels.
Do keep the 2px Machine Yellow focus ring on every interactive element.
Do put a word, dot or numbered marker beside every status tone, and format every figure with formatNumber for the active language.
Do keep a 44px minimum target for every control at 900px and below.
donts: Don't gamify. No celebratory progress fills, no status emojis, no green glow because a number went up.
Don't polish into a SaaS dashboard. No soft white cards, no gentle floating shadows, no generous corner radii.
Don't build a game. No neon, no cinematic bloom, no particles, no dramatic sky.
Don't invent a type scale. Fixed absolute pixels, tabular figures, and the existing steps.
Don't let a shadow appear without a state to name.
Don't reuse a status colour for anything but its assigned condition, and never use one to tell sensors apart.
Don't mark a status with a one-sided coloured strip. Use the full border plus a dot or word.
Don't quietly approximate the 980E. Validation covers the 930E and GDY106 only.
